global_requirements.requirement: All required artifacts for Part 1 and Part 2 must be submitted.
The submitted artifacts must be readable and accessible in the required formats.
Part 1 must include both the OWL ontology and the accompanying report.
The ontology must be logically consistent and must load successfully in a compatible ontology editor or reasoner.
The report must describe and justify the ontology design presented in the submitted OWL artifact.
Part 2 must be completed using the supplied Prolog and modal logic framework.
The submitted Prolog source must load without syntax errors.
Answers for Tasks 1 to 4 must be implemented in their required answer predicates using the formula constructors supported by the supplied framework.
Each formula submitted for Tasks 1 to 4 must express the semantic constraint described by the corresponding task.
Task 5 must contain three distinct problem-and-solution examples implemented in the required answer predicates.
Each Task 5 preventive formula must correspond to the problem described in the same example.

part_2_environment.summary: Modal logic interpreted over a rectangular grid of states.

atomic_propositions.bread: Bread is present at the current state.
atomic_propositions.filling: Filling is present at the current state.

modal_operators.dia(R,F): Formula F holds at some state reachable by relation R.
modal_operators.box(R,F): Formula F holds at every state reachable by relation R.

evaluation_policy: Evaluate formulas according to the supplied Prolog semantics.
Do not assume spatial meanings beyond the supplied rel/3 definitions.

specification_notes.issue: The assessment brief's detailed marking guidance refers to predicates and examples that do not appear in the supplied Prolog starter code.
specification_notes.resolution: The supplied Prolog file is treated as the authoritative specification for Tasks 1–5.
specification_notes.evaluation_guidance: Evaluate answers according to the supplied predicates, relations and task descriptions rather than the inconsistent examples in the assessment brief.

task.description: Develop an OWL ontology modelling the sandwich domain and submit an accompanying report describing the ontology design and implementation.

evaluation_requirements.requirement: The ontology contains at least ten relevant and appropriately varied classes.
Subclass relationships are logically justified and appropriately modelled.
The ontology contains at least five meaningful object and/or data properties.
Property domains, ranges, hierarchies, and characteristics are correctly modelled where appropriate.
The ontology contains one logically correct Description Logic axiom using a number restriction.
The ontology is logically coherent and internally consistent.
The report accurately describes the submitted ontology.
The report clearly explains the purpose and scope of the ontology.
The report justifies the chosen class and property hierarchies.
The report correctly explains the Description Logic axiom and relates it to the source text.
The report critically discusses the strengths and limitations of the ontology.
The report does not exceed the specified word limit of 750 words.

task.description: Write a modal logic formula expressing that bread and filling cannot occupy the same grid state.

semantic_goal.interpretation: No grid state may satisfy both bread and filling simultaneously.

expected_properties: The formula expresses mutual exclusion.
The formula applies locally to every grid state.
The formula is compatible with the supplied modal logic language.

evaluation_requirements.requirement: The formula correctly prevents bread and filling from holding simultaneously.
The formula captures the intended meaning of mutual exclusivity.
The submitted formula is well formed according to the supplied modal logic syntax.
The answer is provided in the required predicate answer1/1.

ignore_superficial_differences: Equivalent use of implication or negation

components.title: Bread Immediately Above and Below Filling

task.description: Write a modal logic formula expressing that every state containing filling has bread immediately above it and immediately below it.

semantic_goal.interpretation: Whenever filling occurs, bread must occupy the immediately adjacent states above and below.

expected_properties: The requirement is conditional on the presence of filling.
Both immediate neighbours are required.
Immediate adjacency is expressed using the supplied relations.
The formula is compatible with the supplied modal logic language.

evaluation_requirements.requirement: The bread requirement is correctly conditioned on the presence of filling.
The formula requires bread immediately above filling.
The formula requires bread immediately below filling.
The formula expresses immediate adjacency rather than arbitrary vertical distance.
The modal operators are used consistently with the supplied framework.
The submitted formula is well formed according to the supplied modal logic syntax.
The answer is provided in the required predicate answer2/1.

ignore_superficial_differences: Alternative but logically equivalent nesting of conjunctions

components.title: No Bread More Than One Row Below Filling

task.description: Write a modal logic formula expressing that bread must not occur more than one row below a state containing filling.

permitted_configuration: Bread may occur immediately below filling.
prohibited_configuration: Bread occurring beyond the immediately adjacent lower row.
semantic_goal.interpretation: The formula should distinguish immediate adjacency from greater vertical distances below a filling state.

expected_properties: The restriction is conditional on the presence of filling.
Immediate bread below filling remains permitted.
Bread located further below filling is prohibited.
The formula correctly represents vertical distance using the supplied modal relations.
The formula is compatible with the supplied modal logic language.

evaluation_requirements.requirement: The distance restriction is correctly conditioned on the presence of filling.
The formula distinguishes immediate adjacency from greater vertical distance.
The formula does not incorrectly prohibit bread immediately below filling.
The formula prevents bread from occurring more than one row below filling.
The modal operators correctly express the intended spatial constraint.
The submitted formula is well formed according to the supplied modal logic syntax.
The answer is provided in the required predicate answer3/1.

ignore_superficial_differences: Alternative logically equivalent nesting of operators

task.description: Write a modal logic formula expressing that if a state contains filling, then no state anywhere above it may also contain filling.

semantic_goal.interpretation: Whenever filling occurs, all states above it must not contain filling.

expected_properties: The restriction is conditional on the presence of filling.
The constraint applies to every state above, not only the immediately adjacent state.
The formula represents a global vertical constraint using the supplied modal relations.
The formula is compatible with the supplied modal logic language.

evaluation_requirements.requirement: The restriction is correctly conditioned on the presence of filling.
The formula applies to all relevant states above the current filling state rather than only the immediately adjacent state.
The formula prevents filling from occurring anywhere above another filling state.
The modal operators correctly express the intended spatial constraint.
The submitted formula is well formed according to the supplied modal logic syntax.
The answer is provided in the required predicate answer4/1.

ignore_superficial_differences: Alternative but logically equivalent use of necessity and possibility operators

task.description: Identify three different sandwich configurations that satisfy the constraints from Tasks 1–4 but could reasonably be argued not to represent proper sandwiches. For each configuration, provide a natural-language description and a modal logic formula that prevents the configuration.

example_structure.problem_description: Describe a configuration that satisfies Tasks 1–4 but should not be considered a proper sandwich.
example_structure.preventive_formula: Provide a modal logic formula that rules out the described configuration.
example_structure.additional_relations: Optional. Students may introduce additional relations where appropriate.

semantic_goal.interpretation: Each example should identify a limitation of the original sandwich specification and propose an additional logical constraint that removes that limitation.

expected_properties: Each example describes a distinct problematic sandwich configuration.
Each described configuration satisfies the constraints from Tasks 1–4.
Each preventive formula directly addresses the described problem.
The three examples demonstrate different limitations of the original specification.
The proposed formulas are compatible with the supplied modal logic framework.

evaluation_requirements.requirement: Exactly three examples are provided.
Each example clearly describes a problematic sandwich configuration.
Each described configuration is compatible with the constraints established in Tasks 1–4.
The three examples identify meaningfully different shortcomings of the original specification.
Each preventive formula directly addresses the corresponding problem description.
Each preventive formula successfully excludes the described configuration.
Each submitted formula is well formed according to the supplied modal logic syntax.
The responses are provided in answer51/1, answer52/1 and answer53/1.

acceptable_problem_categories: Multiple sandwiches represented in the same grid
Other logically justified limitations of the original specification
guidance: The listed categories are examples rather than an exhaustive answer key.
Do not penalise students for proposing valid alternative configurations.
Evaluate whether the proposed formula addresses the described limitation.
Focus on the logical relationship between the description and the preventive formula rather than matching a predefined solution.

cross_component_evaluation_requirements.requirement: The submitted Prolog source loads without syntax errors.
Answers are implemented within the supplied Prolog framework unless the task explicitly permits additional definitions.
Submitted formulas use the supplied modal logic language and recognised formula constructors.
Logically equivalent formulas should be evaluated as correct regardless of their syntactic form.
Spatial relations are interpreted according to the supplied rel/3 definitions rather than their natural-language names.
Responses are provided in the required answer predicates.

general_principles: Support feedback with evidence from the student's submission.
Separate syntax errors from semantic errors.
Distinguish partially correct reasoning from incorrect reasoning.
Do not infer work that is absent from the submission.
ontology_feedback: Comment on modelling decisions rather than assuming a single correct ontology.
Differentiate structural ontology issues from weaker modelling choices.
Identify inconsistencies between the OWL ontology and the accompanying report.
Explain logical inconsistencies only when they can be established from the submitted ontology.
prolog_feedback: Explain incorrect use of modal operators where applicable.
Explain incorrect use of spatial relations where applicable.
Distinguish logical errors from Prolog syntax errors.
For Task 5, evaluate the relationship between the described problem and the proposed preventive formula.
feedback_generation_guidance.uncertainty_policy: If the submitted artifacts do not provide sufficient evidence to evaluate a criterion, state that the criterion could not be fully assessed rather than making unsupported assumptions.

specification_assumptions.description: The supplied Prolog starter code is treated as the authoritative specification for Part 2.
The assessment brief is used to determine assessment objectives and weighting, while the starter code defines the executable semantics.
Students may express equivalent logical constraints using different but semantically equivalent modal logic formulas.
Task 5 intentionally permits multiple valid solutions and should be evaluated semantically rather than against a fixed answer key.
